items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I played with P-Rom's band from 32 to 35.

ctx.x: How did Sales rate in those days? He was a nice, fine guitar player. I just wondered who would be among the best guitar players in town. Oh yeah, he was fine, yes indeed.

He always was a musician, you see. He learned the right way. Oh yeah, a musician. That's what I did. He was great, good. Always have been. What about P-Rom's band? P-Rom's band? I played with P-Rom's band from 32 to 35. I played with P-Rom's band. I played with P-Rom's band. I played with P-Rom's band. I played with with Song that was after that. He broke up the band. Now his band consists of P. Ron's band, when I first started playing, consists of me, P. Ron, Lil' Allegrette Alexander, Eddie Pearson on trombone,…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Well, when I was with him, he had a new band. See, he had got rid of Pete and all of that bunch. See, he had me, Eddie Pearson

ctx.x: We'll put it on the next tape. You got time for one another half hour, huh? Yeah. Then I'll take you to the other building and run on down then. Oh, back to Piran. Who played piano with him when you were with him?

Well, when I was with him, he had a new band. See, he had got rid of Pete and all of that bunch. See, he had me, Eddie Pearson, Joe Phillips, Leo Dejon, Elliot Taylor, and Arthur Dudley, and Alavretta, Alexandra of piano. Oh, yeah. Sales, and Simon. See, that was his new band, you see.

items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: Then we got a guy out of St. Louis, Jimmy, Jimmy Jones.

ctx.x: And Jimmy John, Simon was on bass. It's time to take him sick. Then we got a guy out of St. Louis, Jimmy, Jimmy Jones. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And I mean, them guys couldn't play. Peter Hunter, I told you. You know what happened? Set them David Horn on the left. He stayed out in the hour. Yeah.
He went on to say, huh?
